arithmetic.claim: a run longer than the survival bound cannot be one queue; it must be reoccupation

fires.evidence: 10834 runs of shared occupancy, peak 7 organisms on one cell

silent.evidence: every run has peak > 1 (min peak 2); a cell with one organism is not a shared cell

specific.evidence: longest run 25 steps vs survival bound 13.4 steps; a run beyond the bound cannot be one queue

verdict.reason: the longest sharing run is 25 steps, beyond the 13.4-step survival bound of a second taker, and 99.4% of the organisms present at the start of a run are still there at the end. The run is reoccupation, not one queue surviving

limitations: One seed (20250101). The run length is a maximum over 40 cells and 8000 steps, so it is a tail, not a typical value.
The survival bound uses the top energy 7.37 measured in EXP-56; an organism that arrived with less energy has a shorter bound, so the bound is generous.
This does not explain why the run is 25 rather than 15 or 40. It only shows that a run of that length cannot be one queue.
